pageCache.text:
Dear Parents/Carers,
We are fast approaching the end of term, therefore please note the following dates and information:
Wednesday 15th July: Children and staff will be celebrating those children moving on to primary school in September. Leaver’s certificates will be given to children in their classrooms and light refreshments will be served. This will commence during the morning and afternoon sessions. Those staying all day will have a light lunch. We won’t be able to accommodate parents/carers during these sessions, however the staff will make it a special occasion for the children. We will ensure that children who find this type of occasion overly stimulating are provided with alternative places to play if they wish to withdraw.
Thursday 16th July: Last day for children currently on roll to attend (normal timings for those who attend full-time or part-time Wed-Fri).
Friday 17th July: Staff on site to welcome new children for a stay and play session (new children only)
Those children due to return to us in September, should return on the week beginning: Monday 7th September, 2026. Normal timings will apply.
Please note that staff will be returning the week before to undertake INSET.
A big well done to children and staff at Nell Gwynn, as we received a ‘gold’ award for our summer growing this year from the London Children’s Flower Society.
Thank you parents/carers for your continued engagement and support. We were so pleased to see so many of you attend our recent Creative Day. Hopefully it gave you a good insight into how children are learning through play and the benefits of a creative curriculum.
We will be sad to see so many of our children leave us to move onto primary school. Our thoughts are with them as they begin this transition period and we hope that they settle well into their new schools. Please do come back and visit us when you’re able to!
Have a lovely summer everyone and try to stay cool in this heat
Welcome to Nell Gwynn Nursery
At Nell Gwynn Nursery we create safe, nurturing environments where everyone is known and valued and where needs are acknowledged, accepted and met. We are a dynamic school with an inclusive ethos which ensures there are consistently high expectations for all. In particular we celebrate the primacy of the parent as the enduring educator. We support and enable children and families to develop dispositions to be lifelong learners. Our focus is on building successful learning communities where all stakeholders have a role to play including, children, staff, families and Governors.
Click here to find out about some really great things that are going on in the school and the community
The EYFS is based on 4 important principles that shape our practice:
Our Curriculum
There are seven areas of learning and development that shape the educational programmes we use in Early Years. These are divided into three Prime areas and four Specific areas.
All areas of learning and development are important and inter-connected as shown in our diagram.
These areas are particularly crucial for igniting children’s curiosity and enthusiasm for learning, and for building their capacity to learn, form relationships and thrive.
